title: Underived normalized comparison for native ringed tensors
statement: Fix b, T and adj as in lem-sf-native-weil-tensor-ringed-complexes. There is a record containing an isomorphism from b.native(T(P,Q)) to the reversed ringed tensor of b.native(Q) and b.native(P), together with the displayed evaluation-normalized uncurrying equation for every P,Q,I and f.

source.place: Native tensor model, geometric tensor part of steps 1 and 3; Stacks 06YS, 06YU, 0FPT

proof.text: For fixed P,Q compose the native tensor-Hom adjunction, full faithfulness of b.native, postcomposition with b.nativeHom, the inverse ringed tensor-Hom adjunction, and precomposition with the braiding. This gives an equivalence h_I from Hom(T(P,Q),I) to Hom(b.native(Q) tensor b.native(P),b.native(I)). Naturality of both adjunctions and of b.nativeHom proves h_J(f followed by g) = h_I(f) followed by b.native(g).

source.place: Native tensor model, geometric tensor part of steps 1 and 3; Stacks 06YS, 06YU, 0FPT

proof.text: Reconstruct the representing isomorphism explicitly. For an equivalence E, objects A,B and such a natural Hom equivalence h, put v=h_A(id), let c:E(E.inverse(B)) isomorphic to B be the counit, and put u=h_inverse(B)^(-1)(c.inv). The forward map is E(u) followed by c.hom and the inverse is v. Naturality at u proves v followed by the forward map is id. To prove the other identity, take the full preimage r of c.hom followed by v; injectivity of h_A gives u followed by r=id. Applying E gives the other inverse identity. Naturality at any f also proves v followed by E(f)=h_I(f).

source.place: Native tensor model, geometric tensor part of steps 1 and 3; Stacks 06YS, 06YU, 0FPT

proof.text: Apply this reconstruction separately to each P,Q, and use the proved normalized isomorphism to fill underived. Substitute the inverse native adjunction applied to f into v followed by E(f)=h_I(f). The equivalence cancellation law gives precisely the displayed uncurrying equation, including the specified braiding. Thus the uncurry field is proved with no additional hypothesis or derived construction.
